title: BACE: Safety & Workplace Culture - Biotechnology - Biosafety Levels
subject: Biotechnology

questions.q: Which Biosafety Level (BSL) is appropriate for work involving agents that pose moderate hazards to personnel and the environment, such as *Staphylococcus aureus* or *Salmonella*?
questions.explain: BSL-2 is designated for agents associated with human disease that pose a moderate health hazard. BSL-1 is for non-pathogenic agents, while BSL-3 and BSL-4 are for serious or lethal agents transmitted via inhalation.
questions.subject: Biotechnology

questions.q: Which of the following is a mandatory requirement for a BSL-3 laboratory but NOT for a BSL-2 laboratory?
options: Directional airflow (negative pressure) and filtered exhaust air.
questions.explain: BSL-3 laboratories require sustained directional airflow (negative pressure relative to the corridor) and HEPA-filtered exhaust air to prevent aerosol escape. BSL-2 labs generally do not require negative pressure unless specific hazards dictate it.
questions.subject: Biotechnology

questions.q: Which of the following organisms would most likely be handled in a **BSL-4** facility?
questions.explain: BSL-4 is reserved for dangerous and exotic agents that pose a high individual risk of aerosol-transmitted laboratory infections and life-threatening disease for which there is frequently no vaccine or treatment, such as Ebola or Marburg virus.
